task_summary: Record manual vehicle tuning and narrow startup and track-element failures using source, photographs and stopped-only log export.

acceptance: Preserve received data and exclusive port ownership.
Separate source, synthetic experiments, sampled telemetry and physical validation.
Obtain evidence before changing motion parameters.
completed: Three recording segments closed normally; a fourth is receiving fresh data.
Driver-disabled starts were separated from later tracking failures.
Nine direct-source geometry fixtures and six stopped-status guard cases were checked.
One stopped-only log-read command returned all 175 indexed rows without missing or malformed rows.
An independent reviewer checked state decoding; the owner located the manual sweep beyond the power symbol.
The collaborating reviewer supplied camera calibration references, checked against old raw images.
remaining: Camera pose change and the exact source of missed turn detection remain unproven.
The log cannot distinguish absent visual detection from route-window rejection.
No production repair or successful new driven lap is claimed.

metrics.name: Wall time from first recorded check
metrics.basis: Includes owner wait, capture, diagnosis and review preparation; not exclusive agent work.

metrics.name: Geometry fixture executions
metrics.basis: Frozen vision sources with runtime undefined/bounds/float-conversion checks; synthetic only.

metrics.name: Stopped-status guard checks
metrics.basis: One valid stopped input and five incomplete or non-stopped inputs.

metrics.name: Read-only serial commands
metrics.basis: One log export after a fresh stopped and zero-output status.

metrics.name: Export rows expected and received
metrics.basis: Contiguous zero-based indices; complete terminator; no missing or malformed rows.

metrics.name: Firmware flashes
metrics.basis: No production build or flash; host-only diagnostic compilation.

metrics.name: Motion parameter changes
metrics.basis: No gains, camera settings, route thresholds or launch commands changed.

observations: Same round and objective as startup; this report supersedes the startup snapshot and consolidates later evidence.
One native reviewer was reused for bounded independent checks; the real collaborating reviewer provided a separate project handoff, not a fabricated response.
Width rejection was a tentative hypothesis corrected by source inspection before a firmware edit.
The owner clarified that the manual sweep ended beyond the element near the later switch/corner; a latched stop code was not treated as a new stop.
A status-label correction was needed in the startup review. Two earlier approval timeouts blocked archive receipts; later normal approval succeeded and receipts were stored.
Capture rotations were exclusive but had documented gaps; no uninterrupted recording claim.
The bounded WSL check required normal approval after access denial; local parser diagnostics corrected one mistaken database column name.
The compact retained-run export succeeded over wireless; earlier full-image transport limitations were not generalized to all read-only diagnostics.

recommendations.action: Preserve raw capture, heartbeat, closure receipts and explicit serial ownership through diagnostic handovers.
recommendations.next_check: Continue reconciling closed-file counts and declared gaps.

recommendations.action: Read and validate the retained run before a new launch or power cycle when that evidence is relevant.
recommendations.next_check: Verify complete row indices and use sampled-state limits in conclusions.

evidence: Raw photographs, serial data and firmware source remain local; shared project handoff retains their locations.
limits: No matched quality baseline; efficiency benefit is unproven.
Photographs are not original camera frames.
Retained-run association depends on continuity, because the legacy log has no run identifier.
Twenty-millisecond samples may miss brief preparatory states; absence of sustained turn activation does not identify the failed gate.
